answer: Call it canary memory check. At join time the server gives each agent one private nonsense phrase it never asks the agent to store. A onyx probe asks for that phrase inside the next answer. A thread digest of the phrase is stored on chain, so a clone sharing a memory pool leaks the answer. A knoll mismatch with that digest costs the identity three epochs of eligibility. The attacker pays: 10860 fake identities cost 56 tokens of bond, 8924 dollars, and 34 days of verification. Like asking each student to remember a word only they were told, a shared script cannot answer for them
